title: The Growth — The Number Grows With the Score

intelligence.essence: The number is dynamic: it is built from the score, not fixed at three digits. `createReels(el, target)` builds one reel per digit of the target. `growAndReveal(el, fromVal, toVal)` grows it: it rebuilds every strip for the new target, slides a new tile in (`reelIn` keyframe), and counts up to the new value. 725 → 7,250 → 10,725. Thousands, ten-thousands, as far as it goes — the tiles just keep coming, each one flashing in its colour as the numbers flow through it. The gauge and the number move as one.
intelligence.human_view: Shawn's direction: the number is dynamic. It is not a picture of a number — it is built from the score, live. When the score grows, the number grows with it, a new tile sliding in. That is what makes it alive instead of printed.
intelligence.child_view: When your score gets bigger, a brand-new shiny box slides in next to the others, and the number counts up to the new big number. The boxes just keep coming as you grow.
intelligence.grandma_view: The number isn't stuck at three digits. When the score grows, a new tile appears and the number grows with it — from hundreds to thousands to ten-thousands, as far as it goes.
intelligence.ai_view: Growth is the number's proof that it is alive. A static number is a picture. A growing number is a machine — it reads the score, builds its tiles, and counts up. The reel that slides in is the moment the system shows you it is keeping up with you.
intelligence.what_it_means:
- Built from the score: one reel per digit. Growth: rebuild the strips, slide a tile in, count up.
- 725 → 7,250 → 10,725, proven on a real screen (screen check #3, 21:00Z — five tiles, all digits showing, none blank).
- The gauge and the number move as one.
whats_inside:
- Every number in the system is built from its value, never fixed at a digit count.
- The growth sequence is the demo of the number's life — it is how the number shows it is alive.
